Pick based on what the product must do well, then evaluate both sides of the model.

courseTitle: Vector database internals: SIMD kernels, segments and disk
lessonTitle: Why one vector distance is mostly a memory problem
md: At hundreds of dimensions, a distance does about 0.5 to 0.75 FLOPs per byte of vector it reads. SIMD makes the arithmetic cheap; after that, the bytes you move (and the cache misses you take) decide the speed.

courseTitle: Vector database internals: SIMD kernels, segments and disk
lessonTitle: Durability and memory tiers: WAL, mmap and disk-based ANN
md: Turning on mmap does not shrink an index; it only lets the OS evict parts of it. If the hot working set does not fit, latency can fall off a cliff, because each miss is a disk read instead of a DRAM access.

courseTitle: verl: the HybridFlow RL training stack for LLMs
lessonTitle: Backends, placement and running verl in practice
md: verl in one sentence: a single Python controller expresses the RL algorithm as calls on WorkerGroups; each WorkerGroup runs a training or inference engine SPMD on a resource pool; DataProto carries the batch between them; and actor and rollout share GPUs by resharding or sleeping instead of keeping two copies.

courseTitle: Video world models: Genie, latent actions and neural game engines
lessonTitle: Measuring world models, and where Genie 2 and 3 go next
md: FVD alone cannot tell whether a model listens to actions. A model that ignores the controls but produces realistic clips can score well. That is why Genie pairs FVD with delta PSNR, and why its pixel-input LAM was chosen despite a slightly worse Platformers FVD (40.1 vs 38.8): its controllability was much higher (1.91 vs 1.33).

courseTitle: Fine-tuning a vision model (ViT)
lessonTitle: Linear probe, LoRA or full fine-tune: choosing what to train
md: Kumar et al. note fine-tuning can still beat linear probing out of distribution when the pretrained features are weak or the shift is small (CIFAR-10 to CIFAR-10.1). LP-FT is a strong default, not a law.

courseTitle: Visual tokenizers: turning images into discrete tokens
lessonTitle: Codebook collapse: measuring and fixing unused codes
md: Bigger codebooks do not automatically mean more capacity. FSQ (Mentzer et al., 2023) found that VQ's reconstruction FID was best at about 2^11 codes and then stopped improving, at the same point where VQ's codebook usage began to drop, despite an entropy regulariser.

courseTitle: vLLM attention backends: selection, batching, KV layout, CUDA graphs
lessonTitle: KV cache layout and block sizes per backend
md: A KV cache layout is chosen once for the whole model, not per layer. If two backends in one model share no layout, startup fails with *No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set* rather than converting at runtime.

courseTitle: Vision-language models for reading images
lessonTitle: Reading a receipt into validated JSON
md: Validate meaning, not just shape. Documents carry their own checksums: line items sum to a subtotal, subtotal plus tax equals the total, dates fall in a plausible range. Use them.

courseTitle: Wait-free algorithms: bounded progress for every thread
lessonTitle: Herlihy's universal construction: announce, then help
md: Universal does not mean practical. Every cell carries a full object state, and every operation contends on the single end of one log, so operations on different parts of the object (a queue's head and tail) still conflict. Kogan and Petrank point to these two costs, state copying and no disjoint-access parallelism, as why universal constructions are hardly considered practical.

courseTitle: Weather and climate foundation models: GraphCast to Aurora
lessonTitle: Scoring a forecast: latitude-weighted RMSE and ACC
md: Every global score is an area-weighted average. Weights proportional to cos(latitude) count each unit of Earth's surface once.

courseTitle: WSD learning-rate schedules
lessonTitle: Why cosine forces you to fix the training length up front
md: Cosine couples the **shape** of the LR curve to the **end date** of training. You must choose the training length before you start, and every checkpoint before the end is half-annealed.

courseTitle: Zero-copy I/O: sendfile, splice and MSG_ZEROCOPY
lessonTitle: splice and tee: pipes as buffers of page references
md: Pipes are the kernel's zero-copy buffer: slots of reference-counted page pointers. splice moves those pointers between a pipe and any descriptor, tee duplicates them, and sendfile itself runs on this machinery with a hidden internal pipe.

courseTitle: Zero-shot classification: labels chosen at inference time
lessonTitle: Prompting an LLM and calibrating its label bias
md: Constrain the LLM to the label set, read a probability per label, and divide by the probabilities a content-free input gets under the same prompt. Calibration fixes a constant shift; it cannot fix a model that does not understand the labels.
